title: Half-Light ops crib (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick personal crib sheet for the late shift. Not an official runbook — just the things I need to remember and the shortcuts I scribble down when juggling alerts. Keep this messy.

Shift summary (start):
- Checked cluster health (eu-west-main): all nodes green, CPU avg 42%, GPU utilization ~64%. No pending autoscale events.
- Post-deploy check: rolled canary for model-v2.1 at 02:10 UTC (PR #948). Canary latency looks OK but a small uptick in 95th percentile for short prompts. Watch for regressed generation errors.
- Open items carried in: OPS-5821 (sporadic tokenization failure on llm-lite-7b), INFRA-1319 (cached KV eviction tuning).

Active incidents / watchlist:
1) tokenization spikes: intermittent errors in logs where tokenizer returns empty token sequence. Symptoms: request returns 500 with message "invalid token buffer". Frequency: ~1/2000 requests, mostly 1–2am. Action: if spike >3/hr escalate.
   - Quick triage steps:
     a) tail service logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=tokenizer -f --since=30m
     b) search ELK for "invalid token buffer" and sample request ids: es_query "message:\"invalid token buffer\" AND service:tokenizer"
     c) isolate by model: filter by model_name in metadata.
   - Temp mitigation: route traffic away from tokenizer pool node pool "tokenizer-hot" (scale down pool or set weight 0 in routing):
     - update routing config: redwoodctl route modify --pool tokenizer-hot --weight 0  (confirm config pushes)
     - fallback route: tokenizer-warm has larger latency but stable.
2) elevated embedder latency in us-central: ongoing since 23:40 UTC; spikes to 1.6s p95.
   - Dashboard: Datadog query "avg:embedder.latency{env:prod}.rollup(max,60)"
   - Quick fix: restart embedder replica that shows memory thrash: kubectl rollout restart deployment/embedder-us-central -n inference
   - If restarts don't help: scale up replica count temporarily: kubectl scale deploy embedder-us-central --replicas=6 -n inference

Common commands I actually use (save typing):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=team=runtime
- redwoodctl models list --env=prod --filter=latency>200ms
- tail logs for request: rg "request_id: <id>" -n logs | xargs -I{} kubectl logs -n inference {}
- dump kvcache keys for request: redis-cli -h kvcache.prod redwood:kv:dump <request_prefix>

Rollback / deployment notes:
- If model-v2.1 causes user-visible regressions: rollback to model-v2.0 via rollout: redwoodctl models promote model-v2.0 --to prod --strategy=immediate. Notify #release-notify and update ticket INFRA-1319.
- For infra config regressions (autoscaler): revert helm release: helm rollback redwood-autoscaler <previous_revision> -n infra

Escalation contacts (fast):
- SRE lead: Maya Singh (pager) — primary for infra problems.
- Runtime eng: Julian Torres — primary for serving/runtime and tokenization.
- On-call manager: Priya Mehta — for customer escalations or SLA blips.
Slack handles: @maya, @julian_t, @priyam (use huddle if >15 min ongoing)

Checks to run during handoff: (my checklist to pass to next person)
- [ ] Confirm there are no >P1 incidents in Statuspage/PagerDuty.
- [ ] Snapshot of cluster state: redwoodctl cluster status --output short > /tmp/cluster-snapshot.txt and attach to handoff message.
- [ ] Last 2 hours of latency charts (console -> models -> model-v2.1 -> latency) saved as screenshots.
- [ ] Note any config changes made: I usually write them as a short blurb and paste into handoff message.

Temporary patches allowed (note to self):
- For tokenizer errors, low-risk option: increase tokenization timeout in config to 2s from 1s for tokenizer-hot. Make sure to leave a TODO to revert. Config edit path: s3://redwood-config/prod/tokenizer.yaml -> set timeout_ms: 2000 -> deploy config: redwoodctl config apply --env=prod tokenizer.yaml
- For embedder latency: enable degraded-mode caching: put header X-embedder-cache: true at router level for non-interactive routes. Quick CLI toggle: redwoodctl router set-headers --route /embeddings --header X-embedder-cache=true

Open follow-ups (for next days):
- Investigate tokenizer root cause: possibly related to recent bump in sentencepiece dependency in PR 948. Run local reproducer using sample vectors from OPS-5821. Owner: Julian.
- KV eviction policy: tune to LRU with larger maxmemory for hot cache; track with INFRA-1319. Owner: me.
- Add automated alert: when tokenizer errors > 5 in 30m send PagerDuty (currently only logs). Ticket: create OPS follow-up.

Notes-to-self (messy):
- If I have to scale down tokenizers, remember to kick the warm pool afterwards (warm pool has no GPU so cold start for some models).
- Don't forget to update the runbook snippet that lives in Confluence: /confluence/display/SRE/Tokenizer+Runbook (I always forget this and then lose context).
- When contacting Maya overnight: short huddle, then DM summary so she can triage.

End-of-shift message template (paste into Slack):
"Quick handoff from Carmen (half-light shift). Cluster healthy, one watch: tokenization spikes (OPS-5821) — I routed traffic off tokenizer-hot at 03:05 UTC; will attach logs. Embedder latency in us-central was flaring but I restarted replica and scaled to 6; latency p95 returned to ~700ms. No P1s. Leaving these open: OPS-5821, INFRA-1319. Next: keep eye on model-v2.1 p95 for short prompts. Full snapshots attached. Ping me if anything looks like a regression."

If you read only one thing: sample request id that reproduced tokenizer error today: req_20260311_0a9bfc. Use that to pull traces/logs.

End.
